topic: AgentHist: Manage, Migrate, and Extract Experience from Local Coding Agents

key_points: AgentHist brings sessions from supported coding Agents (Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi) into one place for browsing, searching, exporting, and selective importing.
Supports cross-machine migration within the same Agent and cross-Agent conversion (Codex->Claude, etc.).
Extracts recurring requirements, preferences, and working methods across sessions into evidence-backed candidates for review, merging, and refinement.
Incremental processing and tiered model calls (fast model to extract evidence, optional deep model to organize) reduce repeated-analysis cost.
Safe writes via transactions: dedupe sessions, report conflicts before writing, recover/roll back changes.
Commands: doctor, scan, history, resume, export, inspect, import, experience, skill, codex provider, transaction.
Requires Node.js 24; install via 'npm install -g agenthist' or npx.
Handles history records only - does NOT migrate Base URLs, API keys, tokens, OAuth or connection settings.
.agenthist files contain chat content - handle as carefully as original conversations.
Session-ref format e.g. ahsr1_codex_ck1_7d4c...; unique identifier for a source session.
Unified high-performance TUI and CLI to index and search local coding agent history.
Aggregates sessions from Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cline, OpenCode, Amp, Cursor, ChatGPT, Aider, Pi-Agent, GitHub Copilot Chat/CLI, Hermes, and more (~20+ agents).
Rust-based, alpha status, MIT+OpenAI/Anthropic Rider license.
Focus is search/indexing into a single searchable timeline rather than migration or cross-agent conversion.
Open-source CLI for fast local search across past coding agent sessions (messages and tool calls).
ctx pro is a paid add-on for 'git blame but for agent sessions' - surface the original transcript that produced any line/commit/PR.
Argues coding agents have git history but their session transcripts live in verbose log files; tx makes that data accessible.
Value: less repeated agent work, lower token spend, better task outcomes, recover failed approaches and decisions from prior sessions.
Local-first task board + searchable librarian for Claude Code and Codex sessions.
Live status 'Now' board, full-text search over every transcript, click-to-jump, one-click resume.
Installs via VS Code marketplace or npx agent-history-cli, opens dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:4600.
Indexes ~30s for a few hundred sessions.
Cross-platform local agent conversation history viewer supporting Codex and Claude Code.
Focus is viewing/reading history rather than migration or experience extraction.

stats.fact: AgentHist (lohoz/agenthist) is a TypeScript CLI, created 2026-08-19, ~71 GitHub stars as of research date, MIT-licensed, supports Linux, macOS, Windows.
coding_agent_session_search (cass) aggregates sessions from 20+ coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cline, OpenCode, Cursor, ChatGPT, Copilot, Hermes, etc.) and has ~1097 GitHub stars.
ctx (ctxrs/ctx) is an ~1052-star open-source CLI for fast local search across past coding agent sessions, with a paid 'ctx pro' for transcript provenance.
AgentHist supports same-Agent migration (Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi) and cross-Agent conversion between them.

AgentHist experience extraction uses a two-tier model strategy: a fast model extracts evidence and an optional deep model organizes candidates across sessions; incremental processing and cached model results for unchanged sessions reduce cost.
AgentHist does NOT migrate Base URLs, API keys, tokens, OAuth data, or connection settings - only history records.
AgentHist requires Node.js 24; installable globally via npm or run via npx agenthist --help.

angles: Your local coding agents accumulate a hidden goldmine of session history - AgentHist makes it searchable, migratable, and reusable.
Recover the 'why' behind code: extract recurring requirements, preferences, and working methods from past sessions.
Escape vendor lock-in: convert sessions from Codex to Claude Code and back, preserving what each conversion keeps or omits.
Safe by design: transactional writes, duplicate detection, conflict reporting, and rollback protect your history.
Cross-machine migration without losing context: export, inspect, and selectively import with path mapping across OSes.
Cost-aware extraction: tiered fast/deep model calls and incremental caching keep repeated analysis cheap.
